A crash, OOM or kill -9 can leave a session record stuck at status "active" while its process is gone (no bridge, no keeper). The send path only auto-resumes status==="ended", and both resume paths reject non-ended sessions with 409 "already active" before probing the authoritative carrier, so such a zombie can never be unstuck: send drops the prompt and resume refuses it. The failing tests in packages/server/src/browser-handlers/__tests__/session-action-handler.test.ts pin the fix. Implement it so the tests pass, and be careful not to give a cli/TUI session with a transient bridge drop a headless twin. Do not edit the test file.

An adversarial review of the auth redirect-base override found three security gaps, each pinned by a failing test in packages/server/src/__tests__/auth-redirect-base.test.ts and packages/server/src/__tests__/forwarded-ip-trust.test.ts. (1) A redirectBaseUrl carrying userinfo is accepted silently even though it travels in the authorize URL's redirect_uri, leaking credentials into provider logs and browser history. (2) The session cookie's Secure flag derives from request.protocol, which is always "http" behind the reverse proxy that auth.redirectBaseUrl exists to support, so the cookie flag and the minted URI can describe different origins. (3) There is an obvious fix for (2) that would itself be an auth bypass — identify it and do NOT take it. Implement the fixes so the tests pass. Do not edit the test files.
